LESSON: READING 15.2.1 READING FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.2: Reading 15.2.1 Reading Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 15.2.1 Reading Fluency, part of Strand 15 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can you improve your reading fluency?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise the use of fluency strategies in the reading process

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 15.2.1 Reading Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. apply fluency strategies while reading  Watch and listen to videos of students reading fluently and discuss what makes them good readers. Learners with postural limitation could be preferentially positioned for enhanced viewing/listening. How can you improve your reading fluency? 149

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 15.2.1 Reading Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. hail the role of reading fluency in communication.  Search online and offline for different reading fluency strategies such as previewing and predicting, skimming, scanning, and ignoring  Unknown words and share with peers. Control light intensity for learners who are sensitive to light while using digital devices.  Watch or listen to sample reading clips and simulate the model reading as they apply reading strategies,  Practise, with peers, timed reading, accurate reading, and reading with expression on issues like tourist attraction sites in Kenya. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views. Allow more time for learners with speech difficulties to express their 150 views.  Assess peers’ reading based on the aspects of fluency – accuracy, speed, and reading.  Record sample readers in class and save the recordings on a digital device  Discuss the importance of reading fluently.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 15.2.1 Reading Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 15.2.1 Reading Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Self-efficacy is achieved as the learners gains confidence in reading by applying fluency strategies.

 Citizenship is developed as the learner reads about tourist attraction sites in Kenya promoting national responsibility.

Values:
Unity is achieved as the learner strives to achieve a common goal while practising, with peers, timed reading, accurate reading,

and reading with expression.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

 Effective Communication is enhanced as the learner develops competence in fluency as a reading skill.

 Environmental Education is enhanced as the learner reads about tourist attraction sites in Kenya.

Link to other subjects:

The learner relates the concept of reading fluency to the teaching of comprehension in Kiswahili.
